inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement, us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation add-back $53.0M. IR tags no PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation element and files no combined 'equity awards' line in its adjusted-EBITDA bridge, so the withholding-tax component is not included; at ~0.7% of revenue the omission is immaterial (<$0.30/share).
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock $1,018.0M (FY2024 $260.7M, FY2023 $263.0M); H1-2026 $338.8M. Diluted weighted count fell 407.2M (FY2024) -> 401.0M (FY2025) -> 391.9M (Q2 2026). The flat count is funded several times over by real buybacks; the model gives no credit for the net shrinkage, which is a conservative convention, not an oversight. Dividends are ~$32M/yr ($0.08/share).
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted, held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows. Cover-page basic count 388.0M at 2026-07-24 (Q2 2026 10-Q) plus ~2.0M dilutive awards (Q2 2026 diluted WA 391.9M vs basic 389.9M) = 390.0M. The Metrics CSV SharesOutstanding column is the diluted weighted-average series.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-28T20:00:02Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API); 52-week range 68.07-100.96
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted at a USD-built rate: 10-yr UST ~4.2% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~1.1 = cost of equity ~9.7%; ~$4.8B debt at ~5% pre-tax (3.9% after tax) on an EV of ~$33B gives ~14% debt weight; WACC 0.86 x 9.7 + 0.14 x 3.9 = 8.9%, rounded to 9.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality, China pricing and M&A execution risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), the US GAAP default: operating lease cost (~$233M liability at FY2025) is expensed inside EBITDA, so lease liabilities are EXCLUDED from net debt. total_debt of $4,768.5M is borrowings only (term loans and senior notes).
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interest is immaterial (<$100M, ~$4-5M/yr of earnings); no NCI deduction and no attributable adjustment.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF, scenario-weighted (dcf-methods routing: operating company, cyclical industrial -> owner-fcf.md + adaptations). Fresh build; no memory entry. EBITDA MARGIN BASIS: the driver is GAAP-underlying EBITDA before SBC, i.e. management's adjusted EBITDA (FY2026 guide $2.13-2.19B, ~26.8% of guided revenue) LESS the ~1.2-1.5pp of restructuring, acquisition and 'other' add-backs that recur every year for a serial acquirer (FY2025: $51M restructuring, $44M intangible impairment, deal costs; FY2024: $31M restructuring). Cross-check: FY2025 GAAP EBITDA $1,650M + $266M goodwill/intangible impairment (Q2 2025, one-off) + $53M SBC = $1,969M = 25.7% pre-SBC; FY2024 $1,782M + $14M + $59M = 25.6%; H1-2026 25.0% (seasonally low half). FY2025 NET INCOME of $589M and EPS $1.46 are depressed by the $229.7M goodwill + $36.1M intangible impairment in Q2 2025; ex-impairment EPS ~$2.10. INTEREST: the engine builds UNLEVERED owner FCF and deducts net debt, so interest expense ($254M FY2025) is deliberately not in the flows; last_fcf/reported_fcf are the LEVERED company-definition figures recorded for auditability and are not the projection base. Tie-out: FY2025 owner FCF $1,167M + after-tax interest paid ~$197M = ~$1,364M levered-to-unlevered vs component build ~$1,430M (gap ~5% = restructuring/deal cash and WC noise). M&A: growth is modelled as organic (guided 1-3%) plus a modest credit for the already-closed and LOI bolt-ons; acquisition cash (FY2023 $963M, FY2024 $2,959M incl. ILC Dover, FY2025 $525M, H1-2026 $162M) is NOT charged and the associated revenue is NOT projected -- bolt-ons at 9-10x pre-synergy EBITDA are treated as roughly value-neutral rather than layering both the spend and the growth. D&A is ~6.6% of revenue but capex only ~1.8%: $388M of the $506M FY2025 D&A is acquired-intangible amortisation, which is a tax shield, not a reinvestment need; the D&A path fades toward 6.0% as no new acquisitions are modelled. Interest income not stripped: net DEBT of $3.6B, the net-cash rule does not apply. Working capital captured at -12% of the revenue change (receivables + inventory > payables; growth consumes cash).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: guidance-anchored organic-plus path (FY2026 guide 4.5-6.5% total of which 1-3% organic, ~1% FX, ~2.5% M&A); neither the equity CAGR (depressed by $1.5B of buybacks over FY2023-H1 2026) nor the revenue CAGR (inflated by ILC Dover and ~$4.6B of acquisitions since FY2023) describes organic earning power
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 2.0% vs revenue 5yr CAGR 14.0% and owner-FCF 5yr CAGR 15.8% -- divergence far exceeds 30%. Book value is held down by buybacks ($1.0B in FY2025 alone) and the FY2025 impairment; revenue and FCF are lifted by acquisitions. Organic revenue averaged roughly -1.4%/yr over FY2024-FY2025 per the Analysis JSON.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC; interest income not stripped, net debt company): FY2020 560.2 (continuing ops OCF 653.5 - capex 42.0 - SBC 51.3), FY2021 453.3 (615.5 - 64.1 - 98.1), FY2022 691.9 (865.4 - 94.6 - 78.9), FY2023 1220.1, FY2024 1188.8, FY2025 1167.1. FY2021-22 OCF from us-gaap:NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivitiesContinuingOperations (the CSV rows are blank). Owner-FCF CAGRs exceed reported-FCF CAGRs because SBC fell from $98M (FY2021) to $53M (FY2025); SBC is not outgrowing cash flow. Owner FCF has DECLINED for two years (1220 -> 1189 -> 1167) despite $775M of revenue growth: the ILC Dover interest bill and higher cash taxes absorbed the EBITDA growth. EPS 3yr CAGR is on FY2025 GAAP EPS depressed by the $266M impairment; EPS 5yr is null (FY2020 base -$0.09).

base.growth_rationale: Y1 = FY2026 guidance midpoint 5.5% (H1-2026 ran +8.1% reported on ILC Dover/bolt-on lapping; H2 comps harden). Thereafter organic 1-3% plus ~1pp for closed/LOI bolt-ons already in hand, fading to 2.5% terminal.
base.margin_rationale: 25.4% pre-SBC underlying EBITDA in FY2026 (guide 26.8% adjusted less ~1.4pp recurring restructuring/deal costs; ITS margin down 180bp YoY on China pricing offsets P&ST +200bp), recovering ~110bp over five years as P&ST/aftermarket mix rises and China pricing moves from negative to flat.
base.tax_rationale: Cash taxes paid / EBIT-after-full-D&A: 21.1% FY2024, 19.1% FY2025; GAAP ETR ~22-23%. 21% flat.
base.capex_da_rationale: Capex 2.1% FY2024, 1.8% FY2025, 1.6% H1-2026 -> 1.9%. D&A 6.6% FY2025 / 6.9% H1-2026 dominated by acquired-intangible amortisation ($388M of $506M); fades to 6.0% with no new M&A modelled.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2026 lands at the guidance midpoint (revenue +5.5%, adjusted EBITDA ~$2.16B, adjusted EPS near the $3.57 top end) with tariffs offset one-for-one by surcharges. From FY2027 the company grows at organic 1-3% plus a small contribution from bolt-ons already closed or under LOI (Lone Star Blowers, Fai Filtri, ~11 LOIs), fading to 2.5%. Underlying pre-SBC EBITDA margin recovers from 25.4% to 26.5% as Precision & Science (31.5% margin, growing faster) and aftermarket (~37% of sales) gain mix and China pricing normalises from negative low-single-digits toward flat. Ongoing M&A is value-neutral: bought at 9-10x, re-rated by IRX, but the spend and the acquired revenue are both left out. Buybacks continue at roughly the FY2023-24 pace, which the flat share count does not credit.
scenario_narratives.bull: The IRX playbook keeps compounding: the LOI pipeline closes and re-rates to mid-teens ROIC, life-sciences orders (low-double-digit organic growth in Q2 2026) and hydrogen/water demand lift organic growth to 4-5% for several years, and the China pricing reset proves the 'timing issue' management describes. Revenue grows 6.5% in FY2026 fading to 3% terminal; pre-SBC underlying EBITDA margin expands to 28% (P&ST-style operational excellence replicated across ITS, aftermarket mix rising past 40%). Terminal growth 3%. Note this case needs three independent things to go right -- deal flow, organic demand and China margin -- which is why its weight is not raised above the bear's.
scenario_narratives.bear: Organic revenue stays roughly flat-to-negative as it has for two years: FY2026 comes in at the low end (+4%), then industrial capex softens and the M&A engine cannot fully mask it (revenue +0.5%, 0%, then 1-2%). China overcapacity persists and ITS margin compression continues, tariff pass-through is incomplete, and the pre-SBC underlying EBITDA margin settles at 23.5% (roughly the FY2023 level) rather than recovering. A slower deal cadence removes the growth story the premium multiple was paying for; terminal growth 2%, cap 14x. No solvency question: net debt/EBITDA ~1.8x, interest cover ~5.8x, so this is a re-rating bear, not a distress bear.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35; moved to 25/50/25. Bear raised because underlying organic revenue has been negative for two consecutive years, the largest segment's margin fell 180bp YoY in Q2 2026 on a China problem management itself calls multi-period, and headline growth depends on continued deal flow. Bull lowered because it requires deal flow, an organic demand recovery and China margin normalisation to all land together. No going-concern or covenant dimension (1.8x net debt/EBITDA), so the bear is not pushed higher.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Ingersoll Rand is valued as a mature, moderately cyclical industrial compounder on unlevered owner FCF (EBITDA before SBC, less SBC, cash tax on EBIT after full D&A, capex and working-capital drag), discounted at a 9% USD WACC with net debt of $3.6B deducted and a flat 390M diluted share count. The growth path is organic-plus (guided 1-3% organic with a modest credit for bolt-ons in hand), not the 9-14% acquisition-inflated revenue CAGRs, and the margin driver is GAAP-underlying EBITDA rather than management's adjusted figure, so that recurring restructuring and deal costs are not treated as one-offs. Serial M&A is treated as roughly value-neutral. The market's ~19.7x forward P/E on adjusted EPS (which adds back ~$390M/yr of acquisition amortisation) implies a growth premium the organic record does not yet support; the house valuation makes that gap explicit.
key_risks_to_valuation: Organic growth: two years of ~-1.4%/yr organic revenue; if FY2027+ organic growth is 0-1% rather than 2-3% the base case converges on the bear
China pricing and ITS margin: Q2 2026 ITS adjusted EBITDA margin down 180bp YoY; the base assumes recovery to 26.5% pre-SBC underlying, the bear assumes 23.5%

M&A treatment: the model neither charges acquisition cash (~$0.5-1B/yr in a normal year) nor credits acquired growth; if deals are systematically value-creating at mid-teens ROIC the model understates, if a large deal is overpaid it overstates
Tariffs: ~$150M gross FY2026 exposure assumed fully offset by pricing; IEEPA refunds are unmodelled upside
Terminal value is ~55-60% of EV at a 9% WACC; each 50bp of WACC moves the base value by roughly $4-5/share
Adjusted-vs-GAAP gap: the street values IR on adjusted EPS excluding ~$1/share of intangible amortisation; this model does not add that back beyond its tax-shield value
